Within Dacca Collectorate P. S. Ramna, Mouza Ramna S. A. Khatian No. 174 S. A. Plot No. 1162 Nature of land Pucca house, Area .4264 Ajutangsha." 

 5. But leave has been obtained on a technical point alleging error and incompleteness in the order passed by the High Court Division. It is this "that the plaintiff having acquired no right, title and interest in the demarcated '0464 acre of C. S. Plot No. 16, '0875 acre of C. S. Plot NO.17 and .0800 acre of C. S. Plot No. 19 totally measuring '2134 acre which have been included in '4264 acre of S. A. Plot No. 1162 of S. A. Khatian No. 174, as has been described in Schedule "A" to the plaint, the learned Judges of the High Court Division have committed substantial error of law in failing to direct to identify and demarcate .2125 acre of C. S. Plot No. 17, as had been purchased by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by their deeds dated 4.1.54 and 5.1.54 out of land of Schedule 'A' to the plaint and to allot a saham of 1062-1/2 acre to the plaintiff only out of the said demarcated area of '2125 acre and dismiss the suit with regard to the rest of the disputed Plot No.1162." 

 9. It has been stated in the plaint that thus the defendant Nos. 1-3 acquired '3000 ajut land in plot No.17 and .3100 ajut in plot No.16 by different deeds and they also got possession in .0800 ajut land in C. S. plot No. 19 which their predecessors were in adverse possession from long before. Defendant Nos. 1 to 3 were new persons in the locality. They went into possession after purchase but on measurement it was found that they actually got .3000 ajut in plot No. 17, .0464 ajut in plot No .16 and .0800 ajut in plot No .19-in all .4264 ajut land in the three plots. The defendants remained satisfied with the said area and when S.A. operation began, the land been correctly recorded in the name of defendants 1-3 in S. A. Khatian No 174, Plot No. 1162 and the same record had been confirmed in all subsequent proceedings. 

 12. In the First Appeal the only objection was regarding identity of the suit land. It was sought to be contended that unless the specific portions of C:S. Plot Nos. 16, 17 and 19 are relayed by local investigation, it cannot be said which portion of those three plots comprises S.A. Plot No. 1162. The High Court Division observed in its judgment that the defendants raised no objection to the recording of this S.A. Khatian, rather they accepted the same as correct and paid rent on the basis of Ext. 5. After his purchase the plaintiff mutated his name in S.A. Khatian No. 174 to which the contesting defendants raised no objection. The High Court Division further observed that the defendants took no step to relay the C.S. Plots at the trial nor they challenged the framing of the suit on the basis of S.A. Khatian No. 174. 

 13. It will be seen that the plaintiff claims to have acquired title to the suit land on the basis of his purchase from defendant No. 2 following S.A. record. He instituted the suit on the basis of the same S.A. Plot No. 1162 of S.A. Khatian No. 174 to which the appellants never raised any objection at any time. In these circumstances it is difficult to agree with the submission of Mr. Pal that a direction is necessary to identify and demarcate 2125 acre of C.S. Plot No. 17 before allowing a saham of '1062- 1/2 acre to the plaintiff. In the context of the creation of the new Jama under the S.A. Khatian on the basis of which the plaintiff claims title and brought the suit for partition and regard being had to the fact that the appellants raised no objection as to the recording and consolidation of interests under the. S.A. Khatian No. 174 as asserted by the plaintiff, there is neither any reason nor necessity now for demarcating beforehand the area of land purchased by defendants 1 and 2 out of original C.S. Plot No. 17. The demarcation of the plaintiffs share out of S.A. Plot No. 1162 will be done by the Advocate Commissioner having regard to all the principles of partition and the defendants can take objection, if any, before the decree is made final.
